title: Ragdolls & Skeletal Physics 🦴
description: Turn characters into floppy ragdolls using physics assets and blends.

slides.title: What Is a Ragdoll? 🧸
slides.content:
# Floppy Physics

A **Ragdoll** is a skeletal mesh where each bone is simulated as a rigid body connected by constraints. When a character dies, it collapses naturally.

* Skeletal Mesh + **Physics Asset** (bone shapes, constraints) → Ragdoll.
* Unreal creates Physics Assets automatically when you import a skeletal mesh (or you can create one).

*Analogy:* A ragdoll is like a **marionette with its strings cut** – each limb moves independently under gravity.

quizData.question: A physics asset defines how a skeletal mesh will ragdoll.
quizData.explanation: The physics asset specifies collision shapes and constraints for each bone.

slides.title: Setting Up a Ragdoll 🛠️
slides.content:
## From Animation to Physics

1. In the Skeletal Mesh's **Physics Asset**, adjust collision bodies for each bone (simplify if needed).
2. In the Character Blueprint, use the **Set Simulate Physics** node on the mesh to activate ragdoll.
3. Optionally blend: use **Set All Bodies Below Physics Blend Weight** to partially ragdoll (e.g., only upper body).

Trigger ragdoll on death or damage via Blueprint.

slides.title: Physics Blend 💪
slides.content:
## Partial Ragdoll

With **Physics Blend Weight**, you can blend between animation and physics. A value of 0 = full animation, 1 = full physics.

Useful for:
* Hit reactions (upper body flinches while legs stand).
* Knocked‑out characters.
* The blend is per‑bone; you can set weights in the Physics Asset or via Blueprint.

This gives a natural mix without going full limp.

quizData.question: To make only a character's arms flop while the legs stay animated, use _____ Blend Weight.
quizData.explanation: Physics Blend Weight per bone controls the mix between animation and simulation.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Optimise Collision Bodies

For ragdolls, use simple capsules for bones. Too many complex bodies kill performance and cause instability.
